1.explanation:
1. LayerGroup.getLayerStatesArray computes a composite opacity (child opacity × group opacity) and stores it in each layerState.opacity.  
2. However, both the CanvasVectorTileLayerRenderer and WebGLVectorTileLayerRenderer do not read that state opacity when rendering labels:  
   • CanvasVectorTileLayerRenderer.prepareFrame/postRender use the layer’s own getOpacity() or hard-coded alpha instead of frameState.layerStatesArray[n].opacity, so group opacity never applies to the feature replay builder (including text).  
   • WebGLVectorTileLayerRenderer.beforeTilesRender and applyUniforms_ always drive GLOBAL_ALPHA from the tile’s own alpha or even a constant (1), ignoring the state opacity.  
As a result, group opacity changes do not propagate into the shader uniform or canvas globalAlpha used for label drawing. The fix is for those renderer methods to read and apply layerState.opacity (which already includes the group opacity) rather than only the individual layer’s opacity.
1.bug_scenario: When a LayerGroup’s overall opacity is changed (via setOpacity()), child vector-tile layers’ labels do not fade in/out with the group—even though fill colors in the same tiles do. Adjusting a vector-tile layer’s own opacity works as expected, but the group opacity is not picked up for label rendering.

2.explanation: LayerGroup.getLayerStatesArray is responsible for multiplying each child’s opacity by the group opacity and should drive all rendering. CanvasVectorTileLayerRenderer.renderDeclutter and WebGLVectorTileLayerRenderer.renderDeclutter create a separate declutter canvas for text labels rather than drawing into the layer’s main canvas, so they never receive the adjusted alpha from getLayerStatesArray. CompositeMapRenderer.flushDeclutterItems then appends those declutter canvases directly to the map container, outside any per‐layer canvas whose CSS opacity has been set, meaning the group opacity has no effect on vector‐tile labels.
2.bug_scenario: In the sandbox, dragging the “group” opacity slider correctly fades the fill and vector layer labels in that layer group, but the labels generated for the vector‐tile layer remain at full opacity. In other words, a LayerGroup setOpacity() call multiplies into child vector layers (and their canvases), but the decluttered text drawn for vector‐tile labels is rendered in its own canvas outside that per‐layer canvas and never inherits the group’s alpha.
